title: Grateful Dead Live at Community Theatre on 1968-09-20
lineage: CD > Adobe Audition v1.5 > CD Wave > FLAC
source: SBD > Master Reel > Cassette > Dat > CD

ai_review.summary: Good soundboard capture of a quirky September ’68 show with a unique Schoolgirl, a laughing Jerry on St Stephen, and an engaging tabla‑enhanced drums segment.
ai_review.review: The recording is a mostly clean soundboard tape with a little hiss and a pronounced Mickey drum trap, but it remains listenable and lets the chemistry of this late‑summer set shine through. Highlights include an off‑the‑cuff version of “Schoolgirl,” Jerry’s priceless laugh during “St Stephen,” a concise “The Eleven,” and a half‑hour drums marathon featuring guest tabla players. Opinions on the performance are mixed – some praise its spontaneity while others find parts uneven.

ai_rating.rationale: Average to good show quality (standout moments offset by uneven sections) combined with a solid soundboard recording yields a mid‑range rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mostly top‑notch clarity; slight hiss and heavy emphasis on the Mickey drum trap, but overall crisp enough for dancing.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Long, chemistry‑rich set with early ’68 energy; PA issues affect drums but the half‑hour drum segment stands out thanks to four‑percussion interplay.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Laughs during “St. Stephen,” adding a priceless, spontaneous vibe.
band_member_comments.Drums: Guest tabla player and heavy Mickey trap give the drums a distinctive, hypnotic feel; some listeners note the section can feel long.
